question: Observe the following statements : (a) Sagar cyclonic storm originated in May 2019 in Arabian Sea. (b) Sagar cyclonic storm disrupted properties on South Konkan coast.
explanation: The examiner has marked option D. Cyclone Sagar formed in May 2018 over the Gulf of Aden/western Arabian Sea and hit the Horn of Africa — not May 2019, and its track did not disrupt the South Konkan coast. Both statements in the stem are factually off.

question: Research was done at ______ with reference to the Middle Age and Copper Age in terms of human settlement in Maharashtra.
explanation: Working through it, option D is the one. MPSC bundles such Maharashtra archaeology sites together often.

subject: General Studies
question: The father of Human Geography is _______.
explanation: The right pick is option C. Paul Vidal de la Blache, the French geographer who stressed human–environment interaction and regional synthesis, is widely called the father of Human Geography. Herodotus and Hecataeus are early geographers; Brunhes worked on human geography later but the title goes to Vidal-de-la-Blache.

subject: Geography
question: Observe the following statements : (a) Jhelum is a tributary of River Indus and flows through Lake Wular. (b) Sutlej is a southern tributary of River Indus.
explanation: Go with option C. Jhelum is an Indus tributary that passes through Wular Lake in Kashmir, and Sutlej joins the Indus from the south/east after flowing through Punjab. Both statements in the stem hold for the Indus system.

subject: Geography
question: Observe the following statements : (a) Mountain located between Pravara and Kukadi river is Harishchandra mountain. (b) River Manjira flows on Balaghat Plateau. (c) Satmala and Ajantha mountain ranges are between Tapi and Godavari river valleys.

options.D: All the above statements are correct

explanation: The examiner has marked option D. Harishchandra range lies between the Pravara and Kukadi rivers; Manjira drains the Balaghat plateau tract; and Satmala–Ajantha ranges sit between the Tapi and Godavari valleys. All three Maharashtra landform statements are correct.

subject: Geography
question: Which of the following statements are correct about Bhabhar Plains ? (a) The porosity is very high and hence small rivers disappear. (b) The Bhabhar tract is suitable for crops. (c) The inhabitants of the Bhabhar Plains are cattle-keeping Gujjars.
explanation: Straight to the answer — option C. Bhabhar tracts are highly porous boulder beds where streams sink, so they are not crop-friendly; Gujjars traditionally graze cattle there. Statement (b) alone is wrong — agriculture belongs to the adjoining Terai, not the Bhabhar belt.

subject: General Studies
question: Match the pairs: List I - List II (a) Monoclinal fold - (i) Both limbs parallel but inclined to one side (b) Isoclinal fold - (ii) One limb turned over the other limb (c) Recumbent fold - (iii) One limb inclined and the other perpendicular (d) Overturned fold - (iv) Both limbs parallel to each other and the ground
explanation: Working through it, option C is the one. Monoclinal folds show one limb inclined and the other nearly perpendicular; isoclinal folds have both limbs parallel but tilted; recumbent folds lie with limbs parallel to the ground; overturned folds have one limb flipped over the other. explanation: On this one, option B. Consequent streams follow the original regional slope; obsequent ones run opposite to rock dip; subsequent streams cut across resistant outcrops; braided streams split into a maze of interconnected channels. Match each river type to its defining behaviour.

question: Biosphere reserves are demarcated into ______ .

options.B: Core zone, buffer zone and micro ecological zone
options.C: Buffer zone, transition zone and micro ecological zone
options.D: Core zone, transition zone and micro ecological zone

explanation: Pick option A. UNESCO's Man and Biosphere programme divides each biosphere reserve into a strictly protected core zone, a buffer zone for limited activity, and a transition zone where sustainable human use is allowed. The other options swap in non-standard labels.

question: Observe the statements regarding agriculture in Maharashtra : (a) Soil erosion is not a serious problem of agriculture. (b) Soil erosion takes place due to flooding in rivers, forest cutting and uncontrolled grazing. (c) Soils are saline due to over-irrigation.
explanation: The right pick is option A. Soil erosion is a serious problem in Maharashtra — statement (a) is false. Flooding, deforestation, and uncontrolled grazing do cause erosion, and over-irrigation can leave soils saline. Only (b) and (c) survive.

question: Examine the following statements and select the proper options : Statement (A) : Every longitude has a different local time due to the rotation of the Earth. Statement (B) : Standard time system is utilized to remove the difference in the local time.

options.B: Statement (A) is correct but statement (B) is wrong
options.C: Statement (A) is wrong but statement (B) is correct

explanation: Go with option A. Earth's rotation makes local solar time differ for every longitude, and countries adopt standard time (fixed meridian) precisely to avoid that confusion in clocks and schedules. Both Statement (A) and Statement (B) are correct according to the textbook.

question: Match the pairs: List I - List II (a) Dome-shaped Plateau - (i) Deccan Plateau (b) Volcanic Plateau - (ii) Vindhya Plateau (c) Step-like Plateau - (iii) Chota Nagpur Plateau (d) Piedmont Plateau - (iv) Shillong Plateau
explanation: On this one, option C. Chota Nagpur is the classic dome-shaped plateau, the Deccan is a volcanic lava plateau, the Vindhyan tract forms a step-like dissected plateau, and the Shillong plateau is a piedmont feature at the foot of the Khasi hills. Plateau type and example must move as a unit.

question: In India, which of the following has become a hot-spot with reference to threats to biodiversity ?
explanation: Working through it, option C is the one. Northeastern India falls in the Indo-Burma global biodiversity hotspot and faces habitat loss, fragmentation, and hunting pressure. The northwest, Deccan interior, and western dry tracts are stressed too, but NE India is the standout hotspot answer in MPSC environment sets.

subject: General Studies
question: Which of the following are characteristics of Coral Reefs ? (a) These are the oldest living communities on Earth. (b) It is a high biomass producer. (c) It is a rich floral and fauna diversity. (d) These are shallow water tropical ecosystems. Which of the above statement/s is/are correct ?
explanation: The examiner has marked option D. Coral reefs are among Earth's oldest living communities, support very high biomass, harbour rich flora and fauna, and thrive in shallow tropical seas. All four listed traits apply — do not drop any statement when revising reef ecology.

subject: General Studies
question: What is Alpha, Beta and Gamma Diversity ? (a) Richness of species (b) Simpson's Diversity Index (c) For measuring biodiversity over geographical scale (d) Whittaker (1972) suggested these terms Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
explanation: Straight to the answer — option C. Alpha, beta, and gamma diversity measure species richness at local, between-habitat, and regional scales respectively — that is their core purpose across a geographical gradient. They are not Simpson's index, and the key here accepts only the scale-based description in (c).

subject: General Studies
question: Match the pairs: List I - List II (a) Andhra Pradesh - (i) Radhanagari (b) Maharashtra - (ii) Bhagwan Mahavir (c) West Bengal - (iii) Pulicat (d) Goa - (iv) Jaldapara
explanation: The right pick is option C. Pulicat (shared with Andhra Pradesh), Radhanagari (Maharashtra), Jaldapara (West Bengal), and Bhagwan Mahavir (Goa) match in the order (iii) (i) (iv) (ii). State–protected-area pairs are high-yield MPSC revision.

subject: Geography
question: Which of the following factors are included in chemical environment ? (a) Temperature and soil (b) Water and soil (c) Vegetation and water (d) Human functions and Biological components Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
explanation: Pick option D. Chemical environment in ecology means abiotic chemical factors such as nutrients, gases, and pH — not mixed lists of temperature, soil, vegetation, or human activity bundled as in (a)–(d). None of the four options states that correctly.

subject: Economy
question: Given the importance of supply side factors in determination of inflation in India, following long-term policies are likely to help. (a) Changing production patterns (b) Calibrated import policy (c) Focus on transportation (d) Storage infrastructure for perishable commodities Which of the above options is/are correct ?
explanation: On this one, option D. Supply-side inflation in India responds to production-pattern shifts, calibrated imports, better transport logistics, and cold-chain storage for perishables — each listed policy eases bottlenecks that push prices up. All four belong on the supply-side checklist.

subject: General Studies
question: Which factor is not considered while calculating Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI) ?
explanation: Go with option B. Morris David Morris's Physical Quality of Life Index combines life expectancy, infant mortality, and literacy — not per capita income, which enters HDI-style indices instead. Income is the deliberate distractor here.

subject: Economy
question: Which of the following statements are correct about the Total Poverty Gap (TPG) ?

options.A: TPG measures the total amount of income necessary to raise everyone below poverty line up to that line.
options.B: TPG is the number of those whose incomes fall below absolute poverty line.
options.C: TPG measures the share of total national income that each factor of production receives.
options.D: TPG measures the relative degree of income inequality in a country.

explanation: Working through it, option A is the one. Total Poverty Gap adds up, across all poor households, the shortfall between each person's income and the poverty line — the rupee amount needed to lift everyone to the line. Options (b)–(d) describe headcount, factor shares, and inequality instead.

subject: Economy
question: Government of Maharashtra has adopted gender budgeting from the year _________.
explanation: Straight to the answer — option C. Maharashtra introduced gender budgeting in its state budget from fiscal year 2013–14, publishing a dedicated gender budget statement each year since. State budget reforms like this are pinned to specific launch years in MPSC Maharashtra modules.

subject: Reasoning
question: Which of the following States had the lowest child sex ratio in 2011 ?
explanation: The right pick is option B. Among these four states in Census 2011, Maharashtra's child sex ratio (0–6 years) was 894 — lower than Karnataka (948), Madhya Pradesh (918), and Kerala (964). MPSC often tests state-level demographic figures alongside the national average of 919.

subject: General Studies
question: Which of the following, according to the World Bank, are critical issues to be addressed in India's urbanisation ? (a) Poor local governance (b) Weak finances (c) Inappropriate planning leading to high costs (d) Rapidly deteriorating environment
explanation: Working through it, option C is the one. The World Bank flags poor local governance, weak municipal finances, costly inappropriate planning, and a rapidly deteriorating urban environment as the core bottlenecks in India's urbanisation. Each listed factor is a documented constraint, not an isolated issue.

subject: Economy
question: Which of the following programmes have been supported by United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) along with Government of India for poverty reduction and livelihoods promotion ? (a) Affordable Rural Housing for All (b) Improving Efficiency of Health Care System in Multiple States (2013 - 2017) (c) Governance and Accelerated Livelihoods Support (GOALS) (2013 - 2017) (d) Strengthening National Capacities in Tribal Areas (2013 - 2017)
explanation: The verified answer here is option D. UNDP partnered with the Government of India on all four listed initiatives — rural housing, multi-state health efficiency, GOALS livelihood support, and tribal-area capacity building (2013–2017 window). Do not treat any single scheme as the only UNDP tie-up.

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following is/are applicable to Gender Inequality Index (GII) ? (a) It provides insights into gender disparities in health, empowerment and the labour market. (b) Higher values in the GII indicate worse achievements. (c) The empowerment dimension is partly measured by the share of parliamentary seats held by each gender.
explanation: The verified answer here is option D. The Gender Inequality Index tracks disparities in health, empowerment, and labour-market participation; higher GII values mean worse outcomes; and parliamentary seat share by gender feeds into the empowerment dimension. All three statements match UNDP's GII framework.
